structure: repos/trade-imports-ins-frontend (INS front door, Node/Hapi/Nunjucks/GOV.UK Frontend 6.2.0, port 3002), read in place. In scope: src/server/app/features/index.js (route registry: dashboard + five address-book routes), features/dashboard (controller.js, template.njk, copy/copy.en.js, view-model/list.js, dashboard.fit.spec.js), features/address-book (list/add/view/edit/delete controllers and .njk, fields.js, copy/copy.en.js, view-model/list.js, address-countries.js, success-banner.js, stored-address.js, handshake-context.js, journey-registry.js, fit/*.fit.spec.js), shared layout and copy (shared/layout.njk, copy.en.js, paths.js), services/ins-backend/client.js and services/address-book/client.js (the outbound API shape). docs/repos/trade-imports-ins-frontend.md read for context. No decisions or rulings ledger exists in the repo (looked for decisions*, spec/ at repo root and depth 2; none found). Left out: features/address-lookup-spike (a dev-only spike, not a registered route), auth, health, common helpers, Welsh copy (copy.cy.js), stub clients, session/Redis config. Facts below are current observable behaviour, with file and line as provenance. Fit specs are recorded as what is proven in that repo, not exhaustively per test.

claims.statement: The service registers exactly six page routes: the dashboard at '/', and the address book at '/address-book', '/address-book/add', '/address-book/{id}', '/address-book/{id}/edit' and '/address-book/{id}/delete'. There is no route for templates, saved notifications, notification copy or notification delete.

export const allRoutes = [
  ...dashboard.routes,
  ...addressBookList.routes,
  ...addressBookAdd.routes,
  ...addressBookView.routes,
  ...addressBookEdit.routes,
  ...addressBookDelete.routes
]

claims.statement: Every address-book page reads the organisation id from the signed-in session and every address-book API call is made under that organisation's path with the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header, so a user sees and changes only their own organisation's addresses. A session without an organisation id is refused.

The address book API is called with these operations: list (page, q, countryCode), create (POST), get, update (PUT) and delete (DELETE), all under /organisation/{orgId}/addresses. A 400 response is treated as a validation failure and shown on the form.
claims.quote:
const url = new URL(addressesUrl(orgId))

claims.statement: The journey handshake: opening the address book add page with the query parameters journey-type, notification-id, fulfilment-id and handshake-token stores them in the session. If only some of the four are present the request is rejected with 400 'Incomplete journey handshake'; an unknown journey type returns 404. If none are present any stored handshake is cleared.

The only known journey type is 'gbn-ag'. Its return URL is the animals frontend live-animals set base plus '/notifications/<notification-id>/address-return?fulfilment-id=<fulfilment-id>', with 'handshake-token' and, after a save, 'addressId' added as query parameters.
claims.quote:
const RETURN_PATH_TEMPLATE =
  '/notifications/{notification-id}/address-return?fulfilment-id={fulfilment-id}'

claims.statement: Within a handshake the add-address page carries the four handshake values as hidden fields; its cancel button reads 'Cancel and return to address page' and returns to the animals frontend; a successful save redirects to the animals frontend with the new address id and shows no success banner in the INS.
claims.quote: cancelToJourney: 'Cancel and return to address page'

claims.statement: Only the add-address page takes part in the handshake. The address book list, view, edit and delete pages do not read it, and there is no 'choose an existing address' page in the INS: choosing an address for a notification is not offered here.
claims.note: Looked in features/address-book list, view, edit and delete controllers and the route registry for any handshake use or selection page and found none. Only add.controller.js calls syncHandshakeContext/resolveHandshakeContext.
